title: Convergent structures recur because they are common among programs, not optimal

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Convergent structures recur because they are common among programs, not optimal

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When similar complex structures arise independently in very different organisms, this is because those structures are common outputs of programs of certain kinds, not because they are optimal.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the reason certain structures appear repeatedly is just that they are somehow common among programs of certain kinds

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Fundamental Issues in Biology” (from p. 383), p. 397. Scope: convergent evolution

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-17: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.31

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Phylogenies and morphology can identify recurrence but do not discriminate developmental commonness from adaptive optimality. The required baseline over programs is undefined and lineage-specific causal data are sparse. New developmental and fitness studies would be necessary.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For independently evolved structures, estimate their frequency under an explicit distribution of developmental programs and measure fitness effects in each lineage. Recurrence despite rarity in program space and consistent adaptive advantage would refute the proposed explanation; common program outputs without advantage would support it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Developmental accessibility and optimality can jointly cause convergence.

There is no agreed probability distribution over possible developmental programs.

Fitness and developmental mechanism data are absent for most convergences.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.22
discriminating power: 0.18
data existence: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Independent origins can be read from public phylogenies, and the frequency of a pattern among small programs can be counted. Those two measurements do not decide between a shared developmental attractor and selection for performance, because both predict recurrence. The claim is only partly discriminated, and only for structures that have been functionally compared.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For structures that arose more than once, estimate how often short programs of the relevant class emit that structure, and compare functional performance with alternatives that do not recur. Recurrence of structures that are common in the program sample and not superior in performance would support the claim; recurrence only of structures that outperform alternatives would favor optimality.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Optimality and historical availability are both compatible with the same repeated structure.

Common in program space depends on the class of programs one samples.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.32
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.45
